account:
It is six in the morning on day 1, and I have just woken at home. Today I am due at the office at eight, the mill for a grain inspection at ten, home for lunch, the office for council letters at one, tea with my neighbour at three, back at the office at four-thirty, and home at seven. I should read the appointment book this morning to confirm these arrangements.

The unusual business is the lighting and bread being assembled in the town hall. Yesterday I personally saw builder deposit bread in the chest at the eastern table, and later saw innkeeper add bread there too. Secretary saw lanterns being placed and has been trying to establish the arrangements, but has not confirmed an occasion or obtained builder's explanation. My neighbour also relayed a report from Townsfolk Two about lights at the bakery, though neither my neighbour nor I verified that. According to my neighbour, builder described his work as ordinary supplies and hall lighting.

Taken together, the hall lighting and deliveries suggest preparations for some communal meal or gathering, possibly a celebration, but that is only my inference. I do not know its purpose, timing, or who has organized it beyond builder's reported coordination of supplies and lighting. Nor do I know that anyone is deliberately keeping it from me: people have repeatedly left before questions could be answered. Secretary has promised to leave any further information with my appointments. Yesterday's accounts were also unavailable, and there was no correspondence or request to see me reported by late afternoon. I want to check the morning record and ask builder or innkeeper directly rather than treat these hints as established news.
